1	# Agent Instructions
2	
3	Canonical instructions for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` are
4	pointers to this file and must stay pointers. Add project context here, never in the pointer files.
5	CI enforces this with `npm run check:agent-docs`.
6	
7	## Project
8	
9	My First Commit is a Next.js 16 App Router app (React 19, Tailwind 4, TypeScript strict). A visitor
10	enters a GitHub handle and sees that user's first public commit plus the nine that followed. There
11	is no database, no accounts, and no server-side storage of searches.
12	
13	## Commands
14	
15	```bash
16	npm run dev              # localhost:3000
17	npm audit                # dependency vulnerability gate
18	npm test                 # vitest run (jsdom)
19	npm run test:coverage    # vitest run with V8 coverage; the gate's unit step, thresholds included
20	npm run test:watch
21	npm run lint             # eslint
22	npm run format           # prettier --write
23	npm run format:check     # prettier --check (CI gate)
24	npm run check:agent-docs # verify pointer files, ignore lists, and the gate list have not drifted
25	npm run check:labels     # validate .github/labels.yml
26	npm run sync:labels      # reconcile GitHub labels with .github/labels.yml
27	npm run build
28	npm run test:e2e         # playwright; boots its own dev server on :3100 (E2E_PORT to override)
29	```
30	
31	Full pre-PR validation. The `CI / validate` job runs this same script, so it is the gate, not a copy
32	of it:
33	
34	```bash
35	npm run validate         # the complete gate, in CI order
36	```
37	
38	It stops at the first failure, so a command that printed nothing did not run and did not pass. The
39	commands it chains are listed in [docs/development.md](docs/development.md#validation) and in the
40	`verifier` sub-agent definition; deliberately not here, because a third copy is a third thing to
41	drift. Run the individual commands above when a scoped rerun is enough, per step 7.
42	
43	## Layout
44	
45	- `app/page.tsx` — homepage shell
46	- `app/_lib/actions.ts` — `getCommits` server action; Octokit search plus error normalization
47	- `app/_lib/commitSearchCache.ts` — in-memory TTL cache (5 minutes, 100 entries)
48	- `app/_lib/commitSearchInFlight.ts` — shares one upstream search between concurrent identical requests
49	- `app/_lib/commitSearchRateLimit.ts` — per-client rolling window over the searches that reach GitHub
50	- `app/_lib/searchClientKey.ts` — salted per-process hash of the forwarded client address
51	- `app/_lib/username.ts` — validation and normalization, used on both the client and the server action
52	- `app/_lib/logger.ts` — structured warn/error logging
53	- `app/_home/` — homepage search internals (hook, form, results, timeline card, recent searches,
54	  analytics)
55	- `app/_components/` — components used by something other than one feature
56	- `app/_lib/` — everything above plus `commitTypes.ts`, `githubUrls.ts`, and
57	  `e2eCommitSearchMocks.ts`; no route file lives here and no file here renders
58	- `app/api/health/route.ts` — runtime health JSON for production checks
59	- `app/api/e2e-readiness/route.ts` — non-production probe telling the Playwright preflight whether
60	  this server was started with the fixture mocks
61	- `tests/e2e/` — Playwright specs; unit tests are colocated as `*.test.ts(x)`
62	
63	**A folder under `app/` that is not a route starts with `_`.** Every other directory name there
64	claims a URL segment, so an internal folder is one `page.tsx` away from becoming a public route,
65	and nothing in its name says it should not be. Next.js treats a leading underscore as a
66	[private folder](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/colocation#private-folders)
67	and excludes it from routing entirely, so `app/_home/` cannot serve `/home` however many files
68	land in it. Name new internal folders the same way; a route directory keeps its bare name.
69	
70	**A component lives beside the feature that uses it.** Everything the homepage renders is in
71	`app/_home/`; a component used by more than one feature, or by the root layout rather than a
72	feature, goes in `app/_components/`. There is no root-level `components/`. The rule decides the
73	import style too: relative within a feature, aliased with `@/` only across a boundary — so a
74	relative import now means "same feature" rather than nothing in particular. Before adding a
75	component to `app/_components/`, check that it really has more than one caller; the last occupant
76	of the root `components/` directory had exactly one, three directories away.
77	
78	**Directly under `app/` there are only route files.** `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `error.tsx`,
79	`not-found.tsx`, the metadata files, and route directories — plus their colocated tests, and
80	`globals.css`, which is the root layout's stylesheet and belongs beside `layout.tsx` by Next.js
81	convention. Everything else goes in `app/_lib/` if it is a module or `app/_components/` if it
82	renders. `ls app/` should answer "what does this app serve?" and nothing else; it used to list
83	fifteen files that served nothing. A module imported across route boundaries — `logger.ts` was
84	imported by a route as `@/app/logger` — is the clearest sign it does not belong at that level.
85	
86	## Gotchas
87	
88	- **E2E mocks.** `E2E_COMMIT_SEARCH_MOCKS=1` makes `app/_lib/actions.ts` return fixtures for the reserved
89	  usernames `e2e-result`, `e2e-slow-result`, `e2e-reject-once-*`, `e2e-malformed-dates`,
90	  `e2e-incomplete`, `e2e-incomplete-once-*`, `e2e-incomplete-then-error-*`, `e2e-incomplete-empty`,
91	  `e2e-long-data`, `e2e-timeout`, `e2e-unknown`, `e2e-validation`,
92	  `e2e-empty`, `e2e-rate-limit`, and `e2e-unavailable`. Playwright sets this automatically and runs
93	  the app on port **3100**, not 3000; set `E2E_PORT` when that port is taken. Add new fixture cases
94	    in `app/_lib/e2eCommitSearchFixtures.ts` when adding browser coverage for a new state; that
95	  module holds every fixture and nothing else, and `app/_lib/actions.ts` only calls into it. The `*-once-*` and
96	  `*-then-error-*` fixtures are stateful per process, so a test can prove a retry re-issued the
97	  search rather than re-rendered: give each such test a unique username, as the existing ones do
98	  with the Playwright worker index.
99	- **The browser suite refuses a foreign or stale server.** Playwright's `reuseExistingServer` only
100	  checks that the port answers, so an unrelated app left on 3100 used to be adopted silently and
101	  every spec failed as if the branch were broken. A global setup now probes the port twice and
102	  stops the run with one clear error instead. First `/api/health` for this app's `service` name,
103	  which rejects a different application; then `/api/e2e-readiness`, which rejects a server of this
104	  app that was started without `E2E_COMMIT_SEARCH_MOCKS=1` and would send every reserved `e2e-*`
105	  username to real GitHub — the usual leftover from an interrupted run. A server too old to serve
106	  that route, or a production build where it is deliberately absent, is rejected too. Set
107	  `E2E_PORT` to use a different port; nothing is ever killed, since the port may belong to another
108	  session. Neither probe checks which branch the server is running, so a stale server of the right
109	  shape from another checkout still passes.
110	- **`/api/e2e-readiness` exists for that check and nothing else.** It reports one boolean, and it
111	  is `404` whenever `NODE_ENV` is `production`, so it is absent from `next start` and from every
112	  Vercel deployment. Test and harness state stays off `/api/health`, which is public, uncached, and
113	  capped at what a production operator needs. Read `app/api/e2e-readiness/route.ts` before adding a
114	  field to either one.
115	- **No web fonts.** Typography is the system UI stack defined by `--font-sans` and `--font-mono` in
116	  `app/globals.css`, which is what every `font-sans` and `font-mono` utility resolves to. The layout
117	  used to also load Geist through `next/font/google`; nothing referenced the variables it generated,
118	  so the only effect was a build that failed whenever Google Fonts was unreachable. Do not reach for
119	  `next/font/google` — a font the design actually needs belongs in the repository and is loaded with
120	  `next/font/local`, so a clean build never depends on a font host.
121	- **Three browser projects, two of them selective.** `chromium` (Desktop Chrome) runs every spec.
122	  `mobile-chrome` (Galaxy S9+, 320px, Chromium-backed) runs only specs tagged `@mobile`, and
123	  `webkit` (Desktop Safari) only those tagged `@webkit` — tag with
124	  `test("name", { tag: ["@mobile"] }, ...)`. Tag a spec when the extra project changes something
125	  it actually exercises: viewport and touch for mobile, a different engine for WebKit. Tagging
126	  everything would triple the suite for little signal. WebKit needs system libraries Chromium
127	  does not; CI installs them with `--with-deps`, and locally
128	  `sudo npx playwright install-deps webkit` does the same. **Playwright cannot grant clipboard
129	  permissions on WebKit at all**, so a spec that calls `context.grantPermissions` with a
130	  clipboard permission must stay untagged.
131	- **A new browser project means a workflow change too.** `npm run check:agent-docs` fails when a
132	  workflow that runs the suite installs fewer browsers than `playwright.config.ts` declares
133	  projects for. It resolves a project to its *engine*, not its name — `mobile-chrome` is
134	  Chromium-backed — so adding a project needs the install list in every such workflow updated to
135	  match. Without that check the gap surfaced only after a production deploy, since
136	  `deployed-smoke.yml` runs on `deployment_status` and no local command reaches it.
137	- **Prettier ignores `*.md`.** Prose is formatted by hand. Do not run the formatter over docs, and do
138	  not reflow markdown as part of an unrelated change.
139	- **The commit cache is per-process.** It is a plain `Map`, so it resets on every serverless cold
140	  start and is not shared between instances. Never treat it as durable storage. The in-flight map
141	  in `app/_lib/commitSearchInFlight.ts` has the same scope: it coalesces the requests one instance is
142	  serving, not requests across instances.
143	- **The per-client search limit is per-process, and never a quota guarantee.** The rolling window
144	  in `app/_lib/commitSearchRateLimit.ts` is another plain `Map`, so a limit of 30 searches a minute is
145	  really 30 per client **per instance**, and a cold start hands the client a fresh allowance.
146	  Never document or reason about it as a global ceiling for the shared GitHub token; the cache and
147	  the in-flight map are what actually cut upstream calls. It counts only searches that reach
148	  GitHub, so anything the cache answers is free. What it keeps per client is a salted hash from
149	  `app/_lib/searchClientKey.ts` and the times of searches inside the current window — never an address,
150	  never a username, and never the two together. Keep it that way: the limiter is handed an opaque
151	  key precisely so nothing here can log or key on who searched what. The map is capped, because a
152	  map keyed by client is a memory-exhaustion vector otherwise, and eviction must only ever forget
153	  a client — forgetting refills an allowance, while inheriting one would let a spoofed forwarded
154	  header refuse service to somebody else.
155	- **Logging is sanitized on purpose.** `app/_lib/logger.ts` takes an event name plus scalar fields. Never
156	  log usernames, tokens, or raw Octokit error objects.
157	- **`GITHUB_TOKEN` is server-only.** Never expose it as a `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable. The app works
158	  unauthenticated but hits GitHub search rate limits quickly.
159	- **Recent searches live only in the browser**, under `my-first-commit:recent-searches`.
160	
161	## Development workflow (required)
162	
163	1. **Inspect before changing anything.** Inspect the repository, current Git state, and all
164	   applicable instruction files before making changes. Preserve unrelated staged, unstaged, and
165	   untracked work.
166	
167	2. **Create a branch first.** Create a dedicated feature, fix, refactor, chore, test, or
168	   documentation branch before making code changes. Never commit directly to `main`, and create the
169	   branch from the latest appropriate `main` state.
170	
171	3. **Choose a thin vertical slice.** Before implementing a tracked issue or feature, define the
172	   smallest end-to-end slice that can be reviewed, tested, shipped, and merged independently.
173	   Prefer one coherent user-visible or operational outcome over a broad horizontal layer. If the
174	   next issue is too large for one pull request, split it into ordered slices and complete only the
175	   current slice. Keep pull requests small enough for thorough review, reliable verification, and
176	   quick rollback.
177	
178	4. **Use test-driven development when behavior or structure is testable.**
179	   - **When the change replaces an existing contract, find the tests that pin the old one first.**
180	     A new failing test proves the new behavior is missing; it says nothing about the tests already
181	     asserting the behavior being removed. Search for assertions on the symbol, attribute, label,
182	     or role being changed — `disabled` becoming `aria-disabled`, a renamed button label, a
183	     narrowed return type — and update them inside the same red/green loop, not after the gate
184	     finds them. Skipping this is silently safe: the new test goes green, the loop looks complete,
185	     and the contradiction only surfaces in step 7, one full gate cycle later.
186	   - The main agent adds or updates a focused test before implementation.
187	   - For unit coverage, the main agent runs only the exact test it authored or changed, filtered by
188	     file and test name, and confirms that it fails for the expected reason.
189	   - For user-journey coverage, the main agent authors the focused Playwright test and invokes the
190	     `verifier` to run that exact journey and report the expected failure concisely.
191	   - Implement the smallest appropriate change.
192	   - Repeat the same focused unit test in the main agent and focused journey in the `verifier` until
193	     each passes. Do not substitute focused checks for the complete verification gate in step 7.
194	   - Refactor only while the relevant tests remain green.
195	   - The main agent must not run whole test files or suites, Playwright, dependency audits,
196	     agent-document or label checks, or production builds. After any implementation or review-fix
197	     pass it may run `npx prettier --write` and `npx eslint --fix` over the exact non-markdown files
198	     it changed, reporting only the file count and any error eslint could not fix; these are
199	     deterministic, auto-fixable checks whose output is a fix rather than evidence. It must never
200	     run the formatter over markdown (see the Prettier gotcha above), and must not run
201	     repository-wide `npm run lint`, `npm run format`, or `npm run format:check` — those stay with
202	     the `verifier`, keeping routine command output out of the main implementation context.
203	
204	5. **Inspect the complete diff.** Review the branch diff plus all staged, unstaged, and untracked
205	   files. Remove accidental or unrelated changes while preserving work that belongs to the user.
206	
207	6. **Run `ui-review` before verification.** After the main agent completes an implementation pass,
208	   invoke the `ui-review` sub-agent. The reviewer must act as an expert in responsive web apps,
209	   accessibility, React, and modern product design. For changes with no user-visible surface, it
210	   should say so and return without inventing findings.
211	
212	7. **Run `verifier` before code review.** Invoke the `verifier` sub-agent to run the dependency
213	   audit, complete unit and Playwright suites, static checks, production build, and journey coverage
214	   appropriate for the change. Focused Playwright runs performed during TDD do not replace this
215	   complete pass. The verifier must report successes concisely and include only the failure evidence
216	   needed to diagnose failures, flakes, missing coverage, and environment issues. Fix or explicitly
217	   resolve every actionable finding before starting code review. If a verifier finding requires a
218	   code change, the main agent reruns only the exact affected unit regressions, the verifier reruns
219	   affected focused journeys when needed, and then the verifier reruns the gate commands whose
220	   inputs the fix touched:
221	
222	   | Fix touches | Verifier reruns |
223	   | --- | --- |
224	   | `app/` or `tests/` | `npm run test:coverage`, `npm run test:e2e`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build` |
225	   | a root config file | everything in the row above, plus `npm run check:agent-docs`, which reads `.prettierignore`, `eslint.config.mjs`, and `vitest.config.mts` |
226	   | `scripts/` | everything in the first row, plus `npm run check:agent-docs` and `npm run check:labels`, which those scripts implement |
227	   | `package.json` or `package-lock.json` | `npm audit` and `npm run check:agent-docs`, which reads the `validate` script, plus everything in the first row |
228	   | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `npm run check:agent-docs`, which verifies CI still invokes `npm run validate`, and `npm run format:check`, which reads YAML |
229	   | `AGENTS.md`, a pointer file, `docs/development.md`, or `.claude/agents/verifier.md` | `npm run check:agent-docs`, which reads all of them |
230	   | `.github/labels.yml` | `npm run check:labels` and `npm run format:check`, which does read YAML |
231	   | any other `*.md` file, or anything else under the repository-root `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.entire/`, `.vercel/` | nothing; no gate command reads it |
232	   | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | `npm run check:agent-docs`, which fails if that file exists at all |
233	   | anything else | the complete gate |
234	
235	   Outside the unread-path exemption below, the complete gate must run in full at least once on the
236	   state that enters code review.
237	
238	   - **Unread-path exemption.** When every path this change adds or modifies is one that no gate
239	     command other than `npm run check:agent-docs` reads, the verifier runs that command only and
240	     reports `PASS (unread-paths)`, naming the commands it skipped and why. `check:agent-docs` is
241	     the exception because it is the one gate command that reads these paths at all, not because
242	     they are all it reads — it also reads several files that the table above routes to it. The
243	     exempt set is exactly:
244	
245	     - Any `*.md` file.
246	     - Anything under the **repository-root** tooling-state directories `.claude/`, `.codex/`,
247	       `.entire/`, `.vercel/`. Root-level only: `eslint.config.mjs` anchors its ignore patterns to
248	       the root, and `vitest.config.mts` collects tests from `app/` and `scripts/`,
249	       so a nested `app/.claude/` is still linted and still collected, and gets no exemption even
250	       though Prettier ignores it at any depth.
251	
252	     The gate ignores those paths by configuration rather than by convention, which is what makes
253	     the exemption safe: `.prettierignore` excludes them and `eslint.config.mjs` lists them in
254	     `globalIgnores`. Vitest arrives at the same place from the other side — it collects only from
255	     the three product-code roots above, so nothing outside them is a unit test at all, and a
256	     scratch spec dropped at the repository root neither fails `npm test` nor quietly joins it.
257	     Tests and lint cover product code only. Those lists must stay in step;
258	     `npm run check:agent-docs` fails if an ignore entry disappears or the collection scope widens,
259	     because this exemption is only as true as their agreement.
260	
261	     Membership is the list above, not a tool result. `npx prettier --file-info <path>` reporting
262	     `"ignored": true` is a useful signal but is **not** sufficient alone — `.prettierignore` also
263	     excludes `package-lock.json` and `next-env.d.ts`, each of which some gate command does read.
264	     Agent configuration is likewise not the criterion: `.github/hooks/` is agent tooling, but
265	     Prettier and ESLint both read it, so a change touching it gets no exemption. Being outside the
266	     unit-test scope is not sufficient either, since every path outside `app/` and `scripts/` is — including product-adjacent ones like `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
267	
268	     Enumerate with the branch diff plus `git status --short --untracked-files=all`. Step 1
269	     preserves unrelated work, so status may also list paths that belong to the user rather than to
270	     this change; the verifier must name every such path it excluded and why it is not part of the
271	     change. A single path outside the set disqualifies the exemption. When the change touches none
272	     of `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `GEMINI.md`, `npm run check:agent-docs` is a repository-state
273	     check rather than verification of the change; run it anyway and say so. CI still runs the
274	     complete gate on the pull request; this shortens the local loop only.
275	
276	   - **Unfixable environment findings.** When the verifier reports an `environment` finding that no
277	     code change can resolve — Playwright browsers that cannot install, blocked downloads, no
278	     network — resolving it means naming it, not retrying it. State which gate commands ran, which
279	     could not, and why, then stop for the user rather than proceeding as if the complete gate had
280	     passed.
281	
282	8. **Run `code-review` before every commit.** Invoke the `code-review` sub-agent against the current
283	   branch diff and every staged, unstaged, and untracked file. The reviewer must act as an expert in
284	   TypeScript, React, Next.js App Router, Tailwind CSS, Vitest, and Playwright. Fix or explicitly
285	   resolve every actionable finding before committing. To explicitly resolve a finding, state why it
286	   is not being changed, repeat that statement in the next `code-review` request, and record it in
287	   the commit body; the reviewer then accepts or re-raises it. Approval always comes from the
288	   reviewer, never from your own resolution note, and a `blocker` cannot be resolved this way. If
289	   review findings cause changes, the main agent reruns only the exact affected unit regressions,
290	   then the `verifier` reruns any affected focused journeys and the gate commands whose inputs the
291	   fix touched, using the mapping in step 7, before a fresh `code-review` approval for the changed
292	   state. If a `blocker` or `should-fix` finding survives two fix-and-re-review cycles, stop and ask
293	   the user rather than starting a third.
294	
295	9. **Commit after approval.** Commit only after verification and code review are complete. Use
296	   Conventional Commits:
297	
298	   ```text
299	   <type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>
300	   ```
301	
302	   Keep the subject at 72 characters or fewer, describe why in the body when useful, and do not
303	   combine unrelated work.
304	
305	   **Update `CHANGELOG.md` in the same commit.** Add an entry under `## Unreleased` in the matching
306	   Keep a Changelog group — `### Added`, `### Changed`, `### Deprecated`, `### Removed`, `### Fixed`,
307	   or `### Security` — whenever the change affects behavior, docs, operations, dependencies, or
308	   security posture, written for a reader of the release notes rather than as a commit subject.
309	   Hand-format it; Prettier ignores markdown. A purely internal change with no user-visible or
310	   operational effect may skip it — say so in the pull request body. No CI check enforces this:
311	   [docs/release.md](docs/release.md) promotes these entries into the dated version section, and
312	   `.github/workflows/release.yml` fails a version release when the section is missing.
313	
314	10. **Create pull requests from the reviewed state.**
315	    - Confirm that local verification remains valid.
316	    - Rerun `code-review` only if the reviewed state changed after the pre-commit review.
317	    - A changed state includes code, tests, documentation, generated files, conflict resolution,
318	      or any other staged, unstaged, or untracked content.
319	    - Do not repeat code review when the already-reviewed diff and worktree remain unchanged.
320	    - Push and create the pull request only after local verification and any required code review
321	      are complete.
322	    - Open a normal, ready-for-review pull request by default. Do not open draft pull requests unless
323	      the user explicitly asks for a draft.
324	
325	11. **Merge only clean, passing pull requests.** Merge only after GitHub reports a clean merge state
326	    and every configured check passes. Never bypass a failing or pending required check. Use squash
327	    merge for short-lived development branches to keep `main` linear, then delete the merged branch.
328	    - **The branch must be up to date with `main` before it can merge.** Protection requires the
329	      required check to have run against the current base, so a branch that fell behind reports
330	      `BEHIND` rather than `CLEAN` and merging is blocked until it is updated and CI reruns. This
331	      is the common case when two pull requests are open at once: the second one goes stale the
332	      moment the first merges. Rebase onto the updated `main`, rerun the gate commands the change
333	      can affect, push, and wait for the fresh run — a green check from before the rebase does not
334	      carry over, because it never saw the code that will land.
335	    - **Review conversations must be resolved**, and `main` requires linear history, which squash
336	      merging already produces.
337	    - Protection is enforced for administrators too, so none of the above can be clicked past.
338	    - **Check for an assigned reviewer before merging.** After opening the pull request, check whether
339	      a reviewer or team was assigned by repository rules, automation, or a human. Use `gh pr view
340	      <n> --json reviewRequests,reviews` to see both pending requests and submitted reviews.
341	    - **If a reviewer is assigned, wait for the review.** Read `reviewRequests` and `reviews` from
342	      the command above. If both are empty when the pull request is opened, no reviewer is assigned
343	      and the self-merge rule below applies; do not wait for one to appear. If either is non-empty,
344	      do not merge while the review is pending, even when every check is green. Poll `gh pr view <n>
345	      --json reviewRequests,reviews,statusCheckRollup` roughly every two minutes for up to about
346	      twenty minutes rather than blocking the session; the review has arrived once `reviews`
347	      contains an entry submitted after the last push. When the review arrives, act on its state: an
348	      approving review with every check green clears the pull request to merge; a review requesting
349	      changes means address the feedback, push the fixes, and wait for the reviewer to see the
350	      updated state. A review that only leaves comments is not an approval — address the comments,
351	      push, and then either wait for an approving review or stop and report. If no review arrives
352	      inside that window, stop without merging and report the pull request URL, the check rollup,
353	      and the pending reviewers.
354	    - Merging your own pull request without any review is allowed only when no reviewer is assigned
355	      and the conditions above are met.
356	
357	### Sub-agents
358	
359	Steps 6-8 use sub-agents defined in `.claude/agents/`:
360	
361	| Sub-agent | Role |
362	| --- | --- |
363	| `ui-review` | Web product design review: responsive layout, interaction, accessibility, and visual quality. |
364	| `verifier` | Runs focused Playwright journeys during TDD, then the complete repository validation gate, and reports concise evidence. |
365	| `code-review` | Expert review of the branch diff and all uncommitted files. |
366

I've read through the whole tree. Short version: this codebase is unusually clean and heavily self-documented, so there's no large dead-code haul. What I found is a small number of genuine dead items, two real micro-optimizations, one structural rule violation, and some comment drift.

## Findings

All notable changes to My First Commit are documented here.

This project follows a lightweight, human-curated changelog. Keep the newest changes at the top and move items from `Unreleased` into a dated release section when cutting a release.

## Unreleased

### Added

- The production health check now performs one real commit search and asserts a commit renders, rather than only checking that the app responds. Every other search test uses fixtures, so a revoked token, a changed GitHub response, or a Server Action broken only in production could pass production health and be promoted to a release — `/api/health` reports that a token is present, never that it works. One search per deployment on one browser, because each one spends the shared GitHub quota the burst limiting exists to protect. A partial result from GitHub counts as a pass, since that is GitHub shedding load rather than a fault of this app; an empty result, an error state, or a heading with no commit does not.

- Unit test coverage is now measured, reported, and enforced. The gate's unit step runs with V8 coverage, so one command produces the numbers locally and in CI, and a text summary plus an HTML report in the ignored `coverage/` directory. The thresholds are a non-regression floor rather than a target: they were set a whole percent below a measurement of the suite as it stands — 93% statements, 89% branches, 98% functions, 94% lines against 93.68, 89.58, 98.30, and 94.66 — so a change that leaves new code untested fails the gate while a refactor does not fail on rounding. Coverage counts the files the suite loads, which means the floors cannot catch a module no test imports at all; the development guide says so rather than leaving the number to imply more than it measures.
- Two time-based contracts that nothing exercised are now tested on a fake clock, in milliseconds rather than in real waiting. The five-minute cache lifetime is pinned at both sides of its boundary — served one millisecond before the deadline, gone once it is reached — along with the rules about what may be cached: an empty result is stored so a handle with no public commits is not searched again, while a rate limit, timeout, outage, or any other failure never is, and a read inside the window refreshes eviction order without extending the lifetime. The ten-second search deadline is now proved by a request that hangs: it is still outstanding at 9,999 milliseconds and aborted at 10,000, where the previous test injected the abort itself and so could not tell a working timer from a missing one.

- Partial commit results now offer a **Search again** button in place. A retry that succeeds replaces the partial result, one that comes back partial again says so, and one that fails leaves the commits on screen and explains why instead of replacing them with an error screen. Each outcome is announced to assistive technology.

### Fixed

- A release tag now names a commit that was proven healthy in production, rather than one that merged and was followed by something healthy being observed. The production health check pointed a browser at a mutable alias without ever asking which commit was answering, so a deployment still in flight — or a failed one leaving the previous build live — produced a green run that said nothing about the code it was supposed to be checking. The run now asks `/api/health` what is deployed and stops in seconds if it is not the commit that triggered it. Promotion had a related gap from the other side: it decided whether a deployment had been overtaken by comparing against the tip of `main`, which advances at merge, while a deployment becomes live later and may never — so a newer commit that was still deploying, or that failed, suppressed the release of the commit genuinely in production and that release was never cut. It now resolves the live deployment directly and refuses to guess when none can be found.

- Syncing labels no longer deletes a label whose name differs from `.github/labels.yml` only in capitalization. GitHub cannot hold both `Bug` and `bug`, but the sync matched names exactly, so a label renamed by hand in the GitHub UI read as two things at once: a label to create and a stray to remove. Under `--prune` that combination deleted the very label the file asks to keep — taking it off every issue and pull request carrying it — while the create that was meant to replace it failed with a `422`. A case-only difference is now one label with a drifted name, corrected in place by renaming it, which a dry run previews as `would update: Bug -> bug`. Nothing in this repository could reach the old behaviour, since every name in the file is lowercase today. Two entries in the file differing only in case are now rejected as duplicates, because GitHub could not hold both.

- The commit timeline is now an ordered list, and long content no longer gets clipped by its card. Assistive technology previously received a run of identical card-shaped groups of `div`s with no count and no sense of sequence, for a result whose whole point is that the first item is the earliest. It is now an `ol` labelled "Earliest public commits", so a screen reader announces how many commits there are and which one it is on, and the decorative timeline markers and icons no longer add names of their own. Long repository names, unbroken commit subjects, and URLs inside a commit body now wrap instead of being cut off by the edge of the card at phone width or at 200% zoom — the repository name in the summary grid wraps rather than truncating to a tooltip no touch user can reach, and the author avatar no longer repeats the author's name to a screen reader that has just read the link beside it.

- The production health check runs again. Adding the mobile and WebKit browser projects taught the CI workflow to install WebKit but not the separate workflow that health-checks a production deployment, so the first deploy after that change failed at browser launch and opened an alert issue. The deployed app was healthy throughout; only the check was broken. Both workflows now install every browser the Playwright configuration declares a project for.

A handle can be 39 characters and has nothing to break on, so a single shortcut was wider than a 320px viewport and scrolled the whole page horizontally — the same width 200% zoom produces on a 640px window, where content is meant to reflow rather than scroll in two directions. Long handles now wrap inside their button, which stays one tap target with one focus ring and still shows the handle in full. Short handles are unchanged.

Browsers blur a control the moment it becomes disabled, so activating the retry dropped a keyboard or screen-reader visitor at the top of the document for the length of the request and left them nowhere when it finished. The button now stays focusable while its retry runs, says **Searching again...**, and ignores a second press instead of starting a duplicate search — the same behaviour the partial-result retry already had, so both retries in the app now work the same way.
- A burst of searches for many different usernames from one client is now bounded. Sharing one request between concurrent readers of the same username did nothing about a flood of *distinct* usernames, where every search is a genuine cache miss and reaches GitHub against a shared allowance of 30 searches a minute. One client may now run 30 searches a minute that reach GitHub — an answer the cache already holds is free — and anything past that gets the existing "GitHub is asking us to slow down" screen with its retry, unchanged. The threshold is set where no visitor can reach it: sustained, it is one distinct handle typed every two seconds for a full minute, where clicking every recent-search shortcut you have stored produces five. Counting is per client rather than app-wide on purpose, so a busy day cannot turn the limit on ordinary visitors. What is kept about a client is a salted hash of its address and the times of its searches in the last minute, dropped once it goes quiet; no address is stored, no username reaches the limiter at all, and the two are never held together. Like the cache, the count lives in one server instance's memory and resets on a cold start, so it makes abuse cost something rather than imposing a global ceiling — the production runbook says so plainly, and says where a real one would have to be configured.
- Concurrent searches for the same username now share one request to GitHub instead of each making their own. The existing cache only helps once a search has finished, so a link shared with a crowd previously multiplied into one upstream search per reader, all asking the identical question against a single shared token quota. The saving is per running instance, like the cache.
- Recent searches loaded from the browser are now sanitized before they are shown. In a corrupt stored list — hand-edited, or written by something other than this app — blank and whitespace-only entries rendered as a bare `@` shortcut that searched for nothing, values kept their surrounding whitespace, and the same handle in different capitalization appeared as two separate shortcuts. Entries are now trimmed, validated, and collapsed case-insensitively, and a corrupt list still shows the full five shortcuts a visitor has earned rather than letting junk consume the slots.
- Abandoning a running search by resetting the page or starting a new one now stops it, so its result can no longer appear over the page you moved to and the search form no longer stays disabled until the abandoned request gives up.
- A commit search that GitHub abandoned before scanning every commit is now labelled a partial result rather than "First public commit found", explains that an earlier commit may be missing, and is never cached, so searching again can reach the full history. An unfinished search that returned nothing is reported as unfinished instead of as an absence of commits, offers a retry, and no longer suggests checking a different profile. Copied result text carries the same caveat.

- Vercel Analytics event URLs now remove shared-search usernames while preserving unrelated query parameters.
- Forged Server Action requests with non-string usernames now return validation errors safely.
- Commit results with missing or invalid dates no longer crash the result timeline.
- Unexpected Server Action rejections now use the inline retry experience instead of escaping to the global error screen.
- Prevented older overlapping searches from replacing newer results, and disabled search shortcuts while a request is pending.
